title.narrative: Education for all: Rhetoric or Reality?

description.narrative: Although official statistics indicate that, since the abolition of school fees in 2002, enrolment rates in Tanzanian primary schools are increasing, in practice, the education sector still faces significant challenges. This research project aims to address and to better understand the reasons behind one of the major problems faced by the Tanzanian education sector, namely the high drop-out and non-completion rates among primary school children. According to Ludovic Mwananzila, the deputy minister for education and vocational training, in 2007 “30% of Tanzanian children enrolled in schools failed to complete seven years of primary education”. The project will comprise two phases: The first will be to gather data from primary school children in the rural Morogoro region of Tanzania, and from their families, teachers, and education officials, to ascertain primary school attendance and completion rates. The second stage will be to conduct interviews and discussions with the same groups, to explore reasons restricting access to and completion of primary education. The intended result is a series of recommendations of how the problems, identified through the research, can be addressed as part of Tanzed Tz’s ongoing development programme, with the long term outcome of increasing attendance and completion rates, particularly among girls.
